### Key Risks by Ingredient

- **Dextromethorphan (DXM):** Both DXM and alcohol depress the central nervous system. Mixing them increases extreme drowsiness, dizziness, loss of coordination, vomiting, respiratory depression, and overdose risk.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEShwEBxCJF1za3tgpetvSQEoLajQ6dUSyyQE6VWV5dz4c9bv_FNGFJHd7UrQajeVgorYT4UdpJi8j-oUiYDhPWLwMkQ0n0V9McUid5vprSyv4m-QYHkBOr-FHc_Vz9Q4kz7EQKHVlKGT3zKFxoD7vvbFVOOh-GZ8cD0TDoRoYBYSx-zAdXOXB_Kxw)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScwHEIkXXIY4RwmNqFxXK1yTBJg5Im4UytQtMwqjlgJhrDcxCReQNK7Imi65k7K0EiQryBHWY6WD8lWB3PzQnuBNO_FhfkGyXXLP6a9gBWlZkh1StbYEbEPqSN-VsffFiBbZkBJq4cysxgvxwuPIsIOB_Fng)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESXQHEIkXXdRT_uPZ0DxuUA3xHU1pvUNg2TQE7VSZnL7-LxggrBIga7JEdhBCRAnN_Tt4MQDvPstMGO2pRArFjxIw2kkPgcvd3URU0w-ThtHUFyqzm9j_uDPrxDQnIDQ)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfQHEIkXXGPE0c950X3IcxbSUl23l-A64DIlJu2etQWYoJ11F_DWyCdsLjw1OZ2wauxctDDlEpiyvPwFrDNp44uSS5B9XaDNWdRy5KHUn6HK0QnMO4CmfA5ZIv5pHHhLz7XQNu3JXuULZM0OgfOLV0UPAnEWK7BWCF9jYJ_qn)
- **Prescription Opioids (e.g., codeine or hydrocodone):** Combining opioids with alcohol carries severe risks of profound sedation, dangerously slow breathing, coma, and death.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESggEBxCJF11MZKSCXtaq42E5sBu1Y6_r1AFHQeZl6rRw8R_2pirgsqc_A2BmrrL4rUVWw6iBmeZdb4XdsE95AMuqb6tJYs-9twEAKy6RfXZ07U-d8eQbcXfA8-F-H-EP1Y2r5s6iwigSV9KmikN8kSvoeJNwj34wvZ_brZ0LYpY8qpeWH)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScwHEIkXXIY4RwmNqFxXK1yTBJg5Im4UytQtMwqjlgJhrDcxCReQNK7Imi65k7K0EiQryBHWY6WD8lWB3PzQnuBNO_FhfkGyXXLP6a9gBWlZkh1StbYEbEPqSN-VsffFiBbZkBJq4cysxgvxwuPIsIOB_Fng)
- **Acetaminophen (often in multi-symptom cold/cough formulas):** Taking acetaminophen while drinking alcohol increases the risk of liver damage or liver failure.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfQHEIkXXGPE0c950X3IcxbSUl23l-A64DIlJu2etQWYoJ11F_DWyCdsLjw1OZ2wauxctDDlEpiyvPwFrDNp44uSS5B9XaDNWdRy5KHUn6HK0QnMO4CmfA5ZIv5pHHhLz7XQNu3JXuULZM0OgfOLV0UPAnEWK7BWCF9jYJ_qn)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESggEBxCJF11MZKSCXtaq42E5sBu1Y6_r1AFHQeZl6rRw8R_2pirgsqc_A2BmrrL4rUVWw6iBmeZdb4XdsE95AMuqb6tJYs-9twEAKy6RfXZ07U-d8eQbcXfA8-F-H-EP1Y2r5s6iwigSV9KmikN8kSvoeJNwj34wvZ_brZ0LYpY8qpeWH)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESZgHEIkXXYiJnruDEzYHts_X1MDrzy2IqHGjOi74cb4tAAvep0nWdA9Dev-bKjsbJwEtEJMMyN5ygV7QaI7xUZ-CZXy9ucPAVnKk5zRFeb4jPmQga1Zl6ihTY-AcVrGVuWkqngDTppw)
- **Antihistamines:** Many nighttime cough or cold medicines cause drowsiness that alcohol makes worse.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESrgEBxCJF139Gfn7gFoK2kaKnF-84X9HpiLg1e0eCSW1hgEYnrNchbOeH6gAq_BW71tLHPw-9osisgwSXOTfHYEjtFNyJ9xgtE-D2JYJud1qqlfoqbbF-x6ubDusU8Rlv_sUEEBhwIAT0oQPrjThHgOwhwH783GqkJue-GCLWLqApax7a85P6_6vhSPiWjxzEyMLBWtBUlTff5Z2lbcTJKwg27pFUlPXYFjplcthsMwc)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESggEBxCJF11MZKSCXtaq42E5sBu1Y6_r1AFHQeZl6rRw8R_2pirgsqc_A2BmrrL4rUVWw6iBmeZdb4XdsE95AMuqb6tJYs-9twEAKy6RfXZ07U-d8eQbcXfA8-F-H-EP1Y2r5s6iwigSV9KmikN8kSvoeJNwj34wvZ_brZ0LYpY8qpeWH)

### General Recovery Impact
Even when a cough ingredient (like guaifenesin) does not have a direct chemical interaction with alcohol, drinking while sick can dehydrate you, disrupt sleep, and weaken your immune response.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScwHEIkXXIY4RwmNqFxXK1yTBJg5Im4UytQtMwqjlgJhrDcxCReQNK7Imi65k7K0EiQryBHWY6WD8lWB3PzQnuBNO_FhfkGyXXLP6a9gBWlZkh1StbYEbEPqSN-VsffFiBbZkBJq4cysxgvxwuPIsIOB_Fng)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESggEBxCJF11MZKSCXtaq42E5sBu1Y6_r1AFHQeZl6rRw8R_2pirgsqc_A2BmrrL4rUVWw6iBmeZdb4XdsE95AMuqb6tJYs-9twEAKy6RfXZ07U-d8eQbcXfA8-F-H-EP1Y2r5s6iwigSV9KmikN8kSvoeJNwj34wvZ_brZ0LYpY8qpeWH)For more details on medication interactions, see the [National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESrgEBxCJF139Gfn7gFoK2kaKnF-84X9HpiLg1e0eCSW1hgEYnrNchbOeH6gAq_BW71tLHPw-9osisgwSXOTfHYEjtFNyJ9xgtE-D2JYJud1qqlfoqbbF-x6ubDusU8Rlv_sUEEBhwIAT0oQPrjThHgOwhwH783GqkJue-GCLWLqApax7a85P6_6vhSPiWjxzEyMLBWtBUlTff5Z2lbcTJKwg27pFUlPXYFjplcthsMwc) or [SingleCare](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScwHEIkXXIY4RwmNqFxXK1yTBJg5Im4UytQtMwqjlgJhrDcxCReQNK7Imi65k7K0EiQryBHWY6WD8lWB3PzQnuBNO_FhfkGyXXLP6a9gBWlZkh1StbYEbEPqSN-VsffFiBbZkBJq4cysxgvxwuPIsIOB_Fng) . If you have questions or think someone took too much, contact a pharmacist, doctor, or Poison Help (in the U.S., call **1-800-222-1222** , or **911** for emergencies).[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAEScwHEIkXXIY4RwmNqFxXK1yTBJg5Im4UytQtMwqjlgJhrDcxCReQNK7Imi65k7K0EiQryBHWY6WD8lWB3PzQnuBNO_FhfkGyXXLP6a9gBWlZkh1StbYEbEPqSN-VsffFiBbZkBJq4cysxgvxwuPIsIOB_Fng)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESrgEBxCJF139Gfn7gFoK2kaKnF-84X9HpiLg1e0eCSW1hgEYnrNchbOeH6gAq_BW71tLHPw-9osisgwSXOTfHYEjtFNyJ9xgtE-D2JYJud1qqlfoqbbF-x6ubDusU8Rlv_sUEEBhwIAT0oQPrjThHgOwhwH783GqkJue-GCLWLqApax7a85P6_6vhSPiWjxzEyMLBWtBUlTff5Z2lbcTJKwg27pFUlPXYFjplcthsMwc)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESfQHEIkXXGPE0c950X3IcxbSUl23l-A64DIlJu2etQWYoJ11F_DWyCdsLjw1OZ2wauxctDDlEpiyvPwFrDNp44uSS5B9XaDNWdRy5KHUn6HK0QnMO4CmfA5ZIv5pHHhLz7XQNu3JXuULZM0OgfOLV0UPAnEWK7BWCF9jYJ_qn)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESywEBxCJF1wnduYm_Kp-bbbCuJfJyPkKh6oycS_T02_v9Xbj0OcaORAt5yUQQryVrQ0oGZQ8PNW91IUFrOkeNVWojiJC1E8WKkCWRmCYMU2F4blMK3xURH5WHf7gTuTRPN0DPZkk-yi7ecV7H45Y6CK0bexe8iR-uZy915xsP6rs9fjHMJtBvE8PwfAVpSc6Cq9fg1jvpldJfi0GVTGqSqdKG4KOEwxNyzAqcOXZYB_2finFhjCotJm3R2nkaYxg2AxkWADZK6_nzZyvr9g)If you share the **specific cough medicine** you're taking and whether you've **already had alcohol** , I can give you more tailored safety information.
